prompt: When is the bare prompt's prose reply nearly good enough as it is?

choices.text: When a person reads the answer and decides what to do, with no need for the shop's own labels
choices.why: Right: the labels being the model's own words does not bother a person.

choices.text: When the reply is under a hundred tokens
choices.why: Length is not what makes it readable by a program.

choices.text: When the model is large enough to follow the shop's labels without being told them
choices.why: A label the prompt never named is a guess, however large the model.

choices.text: Never: prose is always the careless choice
choices.why: The section argues the opposite: structure is for a program reader.

prompt: The mean reply was 107.5 tokens under `v1-bare.txt` and 30.6 under `v2-json.txt`. How many fewer output tokens does an average JSON reply carry? Give one decimal.
Why is JSON the wrong format for a note that a person will read and judge?
hint: What does a field take away?

choices.text: JSON cannot hold more than one sentence
choices.why: A string field can hold paragraphs; the format of this course limits it to one.

choices.text: Each field takes away a judgement the person wanted
choices.why: Right: a field holds what the format lets it hold.

choices.text: A person cannot read JSON without a program to format it first
choices.why: People read it fine; that is not the argument.

choices.text: JSON always makes replies slower to write
choices.why: Here JSON made replies shorter and faster.

prompt: Between them, what do the `fields` and `labels` checks require of a reply?

choices.text: Which keys are required, which are allowed, and which values each one takes
choices.why: Right: a schema in miniature.

choices.text: That the summary is accurate
choices.why: No check reads the summary's content.

choices.text: That the category matches the person's label
choices.why: That is the `category` check, which needs a test set.

choices.text: That the reply is under a token limit
choices.why: No check counts tokens.

prompt: A reply is a JSON object with `category` and `urgency`, both from the lists, and no `summary`. Does it pass `fields`?

choices.text: No, because the prompt asks for three fields
choices.why: The check is not a copy of the prompt.

choices.text: Yes: the check only requires the two keys the router needs
choices.why: Right: the summary is for a person, and its absence breaks nothing downstream.

choices.text: No, because a missing key always fails a schema
choices.why: Only a required key fails; `summary` is allowed, not required.

choices.text: Only with `--lenient`
choices.why: `--lenient` changes how the reply is found, not which keys are required.

prompt: Which of the five checks can the consuming program run on a reply in production?

choices.text: All five
choices.why: `category` and `urgency` need a person's answer, which production does not have.

choices.text: `json`, `fields` and `labels`
choices.why: Right: the format can be verified on every call.

choices.text: Only `category` and `urgency`
choices.why: Those are the two it cannot run.

choices.text: None: checks belong to the test set
choices.why: The format checks are exactly what a program should run on every reply.

prompt: The format can be verified on every call; the content can only be ___.
What did adding *Reply with only the JSON object: no code fence and no other text* do for `llama3.2:3b`?

choices.text: It fixed the replies wrapped in code fences
choices.why: No reply was wrapped, before or after.

choices.text: Nothing it was meant for; two other results moved
choices.why: Right: p = 0.500 on two changes, and fifteen tokens a call.

choices.text: It made `t38` parse, since the apostrophe was outside the object
choices.why: `t38` came back with the same broken object.

choices.text: It halved the number of replies that parse
choices.why: Thirty-nine parsed under both prompts.

prompt: Under `v4-only-json.txt`, checked strictly, how many of the forty replies parse?
Why did `--lenient` change nothing in this lesson's counts?

choices.text: `t38` is broken inside, not wrapped
choices.why: Right: there is nothing around it to strip.

choices.text: The lenient parser is switched off at temperature 0
choices.why: It does not depend on how the reply was produced.

choices.text: Both prompts already used the lenient parser
choices.why: `pl check` is strict unless asked.

choices.text: `--lenient` only applies to the `fields` check
choices.why: It changes how `parse()` finds the object, before any check.

prompt: Your program has to accept replies inside a code fence. Where does the step that strips the fence belong?

choices.text: In the program, as a counted repair step
choices.why: Right: the count is the early warning.

choices.text: Inside the strict check, so the test set stops failing
choices.why: Then the measurement can no longer see what is being repaired.

choices.text: In the prompt, as one more instruction
choices.why: That is worth trying, and measuring; it is not where a repair goes.

choices.text: Nowhere: a model that wraps replies must be replaced
choices.why: Accepting a known habit deliberately is legitimate.

prompt: Which of these replies would the lenient parser accept as an object? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: `Sure! {"category": "billing", "urgency": "low"} Hope that helps.`
choices.why: Yes: chatter around a good object.

choices.text: A prose answer saying *this is billing* that quotes a JSON object the customer pasted
choices.why: Yes, and it returns the pasted object, not the answer.

choices.text: `{"category": "returns", "summary": "Ebook won"}}`
choices.why: No: the text between the braces is still broken JSON.

choices.text: A reply with no braces at all
choices.why: No: there is nothing to find.

prompt: Three samples per message at temperature 0, and `t38` failed to parse all three times. Why?
hint: What does the seed choose between?

choices.text: The seed was the same on every one of the three calls
choices.why: `--samples` uses three different seeds.

choices.text: At temperature 0, nothing to choose
choices.why: Right: asking again asks the same question.

choices.text: Ollama caches the first reply and returns it again for the same prompt
choices.why: Each call is computed; it simply comes out the same.

choices.text: `t38` is longer than `num_predict` allows
choices.why: The reply stopped on its own, at 22 tokens.

prompt: Why is a message in the wrong queue worse than one sent to the unsorted queue?

choices.text: The unsorted queue is answered faster
choices.why: It is not faster; it is read by a person.

choices.text: It is late and also lost in someone else's work
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The wrong queue rejects the message and sends it back to the customer
choices.why: It accepts it, which is the problem.

choices.text: The unsorted queue costs less to run
choices.why: Cost is not the argument.

prompt: Which failure does a structured-output mode leave in place?

choices.text: A summary cut off at an apostrophe
choices.why: That is exactly what the schema fixed for `t38`.

choices.text: A reply with a key the schema does not allow
choices.why: The schema forbids it while the reply is written.

choices.text: Valid JSON, wrong category
choices.why: Right: it constrains the format, not the answer.

choices.text: A value outside the list of labels
choices.why: An `enum` in the schema rules that out.

prompt: What is wrong with searching an unparseable reply for `billing` and routing on what you find?

choices.text: It makes an unchecked content decision
choices.why: Right: the lenient parser moved into production, uncounted.

choices.text: It is too slow for production, where replies arrive by the thousand
choices.why: Speed is not the problem.

choices.text: `billing` is not one of the labels
choices.why: It is one of them.

choices.text: It only works for English messages
choices.why: That is a limitation, not the reason it is wrong.

prompt: One reply in forty did not parse. At that rate, about how many replies a day would a router fail to read out of a thousand messages?
At temperature 0.8, `t38` parsed on every try, and `t13` and `t17` each broke once. What does that say about retrying at a higher temperature?

choices.text: It fixes parsing for good, so production should run at 0.8
choices.why: Two other replies broke instead, and the labels became a matter of chance.

choices.text: Failures move instead of going away
choices.why: Right: a retry with a warmer draw is a fresh chance for one reply, not a fix.

choices.text: It proves `t38` was a bad test case
choices.why: `t38` is a real message; the model broke on its apostrophe.

choices.text: It shows the seed matters more than the temperature
choices.why: The seed only matters once the temperature lets it choose.

prompt: Put what the consuming program does with a reply in order.
hint: The repair comes before the parse.

prompt: Match each thing to where it runs.

pairs.right: On a test set with a person's answers

pairs.left: A step that strips code fences
pairs.right: In the consuming program, with a count

prompt: A colleague points out that `v4-only-json.txt` changed nothing and proposes deleting its extra line. What do you want first?

choices.text: Nothing: delete it, since it fixed nothing on this model
choices.why: On this model, yes; the question is which model runs in production.

choices.text: Keep it whatever the numbers say, since it is good advice
choices.why: Advice is a hypothesis; here it was measured and did nothing.

choices.text: To know the production model is the one measured
choices.why: Right: the line is worth its tokens only against a model with the habit.

choices.text: A lenient run, to see whether it changes the count
choices.why: The lenient count changed nothing either; it cannot answer this.
